neighbours.label: Rule and requirement language in technical codes, standards and manuals: how equipment must be sized, rated or selected ('Conductors shall be sized for 125 percent of the load', 'Fuses must be rated for…', 'obtained by referring to Table 3-9'); everyday sentences about the same equipment stay quiet.
fire: Branch circuits shall be protected by a breaker rated at 20 amperes.
Vent pipes must be sized according to the total fixture load.
Anchor bolts shall be spaced not more than six feet apart.
Each relief valve must be set below the tank's design pressure.
Handrails shall be installed on both sides of the stairway.
The duct size is selected from the friction loss chart.
Ground wires must be at least 6 AWG copper for this service.
Joists shall bear at least three inches on the supporting wall.
quiet: The breaker in our hall tripped twice during the storm.
We sat by the vent pipe and talked until midnight.
The old bolts on the gate were rusty and loose.
The plumber fixed the relief valve on our water heater.
The children slid down the handrail of the stairway.
We could hear wind whistling through the duct at night.
My dad keeps a spool of copper wire in the garage.
The joists in the attic creaked when the cat walked.

notes: Round 2 for this pole (round 1 in sweep 4: 'manual text referring to Table 3-9' failed because technical sentences without a table reference also fired, e.g. 'The pipe size depends on the expected flow.' 0.73). Refinement probe: 'Conductors shall be sized for 125 percent…' 1.22, 'Fuses must be rated for…' 0.57; 'The minimum slope … is one quarter inch per foot' only 0.08; everyday sentences about pipes and fuses 0.01-0.02. New label: the rule/requirement register.
